subject: Uplink apportionment mechanics — Aurora Health uptime calc question
messages:

Cc: Perry Lowe <perry.lowe@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discrepancy in April uptime tally — need clarification

Hi Nikhil,

We're reconciling April uptime for our internal ops report and noticed Redwood's uptime calc for the 18th shows a 21-minute partial outage attributed to "uplink provider maintenance" (per the portal). From Aurora's side we had a scheduled network maintenance window between 02:00–02:30 PDT on the 18th; our telemetry shows brief packet loss for ~12 minutes starting 02:07. Redwood's report appears to count the entire 21 minutes towards our availability reduction. Can you confirm: how did Redwood apportion the overlap between Aurora's scheduled maintenance and the upstream provider incident?

We need the methodology because our internal SLA with clinicians uses a different apportionment approach and it's affecting the monthly reconciliation. Attaching our internal uptime extract.

Thanks —
Ava
Operations Lead, Aurora Health

Hi Ava — thanks for flagging this and for the attached extract. Apologies for the surprise on your reconciliation. I'm looping in Marissa (SRE) and Rachel (Customer Success) to get a quick technical read and the precise calculation steps we used for the 18th.

Quick notes / asks from my side:
- Was Aurora's 02:00–02:30 maintenance a customer-controlled maintenance window (i.e., you requested and executed changes on your side) or a passive network window declared to partners?
- Can you share the maintenance ticket or SOC change id so we can cross-reference timing?

High level on our side: we try to credit overlapping windows when the root cause is clearly customer-managed, but when there is a third-party uplink provider outage that causes cascading errors before/after your window we apportion based on packet-level connectivity and our upstream provider's outage window. We'll be explicit about the math and provide a breakdown.

I'll aim to get a preliminary reply by EOD today.

—Nikhil

Subject: Re: Discrepancy in April uptime tally — technical breakdown attached

Hi Ava — following up with the technical breakdown. I pulled service-side telemetry and our upstream peer outage timeline. Key points: 

1) Timeline (all PDT):
- 01:58 — Aurora scheduled window begins (reported)
- 02:07 — packet loss spikes observed at our edge (this aligns with your telemetry)
- 02:18 — our upstream uplink provider (EdgeLink) reported a route flap and started their incident; EdgeLink notation shows their full mitigation concluded at 02:29
- 02:32 — Aurora's scheduled window ends (reported)

2) How we calculate apportionment:
- We compute an element-level availability timeline (per-route). For each minute of degraded service we annotate a primary cause: customer-initiated (if change logs / BGP withdrawals originated from customer's ASN or authenticated maintenance ticket) OR third-party (if our upstream reported outage and we observe correlated BGP changes or loss patterns).
- When windows overlap, we attribute minutes to the actor with the earliest provable impact on our ingress/egress path. If a third-party route flap precedes a customer change, the minute is marked third-party for apportionment.
- For partial degradations (non-zero success but higher latency/loss) we apply a degradation factor rather than full outage credit. In this case we used per-minute loss % to scale the minute's contribution.

3) Why you see 21 minutes:
- The per-minute trace shows measurable loss between 02:07–02:28 (22 minutes). EdgeLink's incident window begins at 02:18 but their route instability started earlier (02:07) in the telemetry we receive. Aurora's maintenance window extends to 02:32, but because the earliest measured degradation aligns with the upstream instability at 02:07, several minutes before your reported change activity, our algorithm attributes most of the overlap to the uplink provider. We then applied a scaled reduction for minutes where the packet success rate was 40–75% rather than full outage. See attached packet-trace and the excerpt of the calculation.

Attachments: packet-trace-20270418.txt, redwood-sla-excerpt.pdf

If you have authenticated change ids showing Aurora-initiated BGP withdraws at 02:05 or earlier, that would change the attribution.

—Marissa
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — that was helpful. Attaching our change ticket and netops log; our change was an internal router config push that started at 02:00 and completed at 02:06 (change id CHG-48721). Our internal packet capture does show the first packet loss spike at 02:07, which is after our config push finished. We understand EdgeLink can have transient issues, but given that the timing is so tight we want clarity on the minutes that were mapped exclusively to EdgeLink vs mapped jointly and how the scaled degradation factor was applied so we can reconcile to our internal reporting.

Files attached: CHG-48721.pdf, aurora-netlog-20270418.zip (excerpted in the CSV we sent).

We'd like a clear per-minute CSV showing: minute, observed loss%, primary attribution (Aurora | EdgeLink | Redwood), and applied weight used by Redwood in the final uptime calc. Can you produce that view? If Redwood will treat the early minutes as third-party but provide a transparent minute-by-minute breakdown, that will be sufficient for us to accept the outcome. If not, we'll escalate formally.

—Ava
Operations Lead, Aurora Health
[attachment: CHG-48721.pdf (PDF)]

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 16:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discrepancy in April uptime tally — Aurora requested per-minute breakdown

Ava — thanks for sending the change ticket. We ran the per-minute reconciliation you requested and attached the CSV to the ticket in HubSpot (link below). Summary and next steps: 

Summary
- Per-minute CSV created: each row has minute, loss%, primary attribution, applied weight. (Link: https://hub.redwood.ai/tickets/HT-4129 — CSV export is on the ticket.)
- For 02:00–02:06 — no material packet loss observed at our egress; minutes marked Aurora (customer maintenance) and weighted as "maintenance-excluded" per Section 4.2 of the SLA.
- For 02:07–02:17 — loss spikes measured at our edge prior to EdgeLink's incident report; minutes primarily attributed to third-party uplink (EdgeLink) and weighted by measured loss (scaled).
- For 02:18–02:28 — EdgeLink declared incident window; still third-party attribution.
- For 02:29–02:32 — residual noise, mixed attribution; we applied fractional weighting consistent with the earlier minutes.

Provisional resolution offer
- Because this is a borderline overlap and we value the partnership, I'm proposing a provisional apportionment: we will apply a 60/40 split of the disputed minutes (02:07–02:12) in Aurora's favor pending your formal acceptance of the breakdown. That reduces the effective billed downtime from 21 minutes to 12 minutes for the month. If you accept, I'll route a one-time credit for April in the billing ticket and record the agreed minutes in the mutual action log.

Next steps / ask
- Please confirm acceptance of the provisional split by replying to this thread before EOD Tue 2027-04-27.
- If accepted, Billing will issue the credit in the next invoice cycle and we'll attach the minute-level CSV to the audit folder.

Link to ticket (CSV and attachments): https://hub.redwood.ai/tickets/HT-4129
Drive audit folder: https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/audit/aurora-2027-q1/
